mathematical_premises.scope: For independent cap-one X,Y, b!=0, T=aX^2+2bXY+2uX+2vY+k has ||p_T||_p <= p|b|^{-1+1/p} for 1<p<infinity.
A measurable mixture of conditional L^p*L^q convolutions with integrable conjugate norm product has a canonical C_0 density and the averaged height bound.

new_results: Endpoint rough-mixture theorem: an L^infinity probability-density factor convolved with an arbitrary L^1 probability-density factor is C_0, and measurable mixtures preserve C_0 under an integrable conditional height envelope.

Physical diagonal triple: three nonzero mutually uncoupled original-coordinate squares, with a same-sign pair a_i,a_j, give p_Q in C_0 and ||p_Q||_infinity <= pi/sqrt(|a_i a_j|), uniformly over arbitrary outside couplings after conditioning.

Near-null double-pivot branch: physical block [[a,b,0,0],[b,0,0,0],[0,0,gamma,c],[0,0,c,0]] gives p_Q in C_0 and ||p_Q||_infinity <= p q |b|^(-1/q)|c|^(-1/p), hence <=4/sqrt(|bc|) at p=q=2, uniformly in gamma including nonzero near-null gamma.
If b^2>=|a|+1 and |c|>=1, the double-pivot block itself has at least three eigenvalues of modulus at least one; every ambient extension is target-valid and has density height <=4.
partner_result_actually_applied: account04/B15 pivot Lp theorem applied separately to the (X,Y) and (Z,U) original-coordinate pairs, followed by account04/B15 rough-mixture C0 theorem.
unresolved_implication: The bare three-large-eigenvalue condition does not force the sparse two-pair physical block. Dense transverse couplings between the two smoothing pairs remain unpaid.
next_step: Seek a grouped two-bank Lp convolution/conditional-height estimate that tolerates nonzero cross-pair couplings while preserving original-coordinate product provenance, or apply a proved matrix decomposition that sends those couplings to another certified branch.
